questions.title: substantial, manageable, pursue
questions.question: What criteria should you use when choosing a multi-step project for the AI Fluency course?
options: The project should be substantial enough to involve multiple tasks, yet manageable within about an hour.
It should consist of a single word query with zero subtasks.
It must require five years of full-time development and a team of fifty engineers.
questions.feedback: The course recommends selecting a project that is substantial enough to require diverse cognitive tasks (such as researching, drafting, structuring, and reviewing), yet manageable enough to complete within about one hour of focused work. Choosing something you genuinely care to pursue ensures meaningful engagement. The {{opt:c}} option is absurdly oversized for a course exercise. The {{opt:b}} option fails to provide enough structural complexity to practice delegation. A well-scoped project gives you realistic opportunities to test automation, augmentation, and human review.

questions.title: breakdown, through the lens of
questions.question: What is the purpose of conducting a task breakdown before delegating to an AI assistant?
options: To delete all project requirements and start over with no goals.
To divide complex work into discrete steps and evaluate each through the lens of delegation.
To force the AI model to write the entire application in binary machine code.
questions.feedback: A task breakdown decomposes an ambitious project into clear, modular subtasks. By analyzing each subtask through the lens of delegation, you can deliberately decide whether it should be automated, explored collaboratively through augmentation, handled by an autonomous agent, or reserved exclusively for human judgment. The {{opt:a}} option is counterproductive. The {{opt:c}} option is a technical absurdity. In software engineering, breaking an epic into small user stories allows developers to delegate routine boilerplate to coding assistants while maintaining architectural control. This structural clarity ensures that every contributor, human or AI, understands their exact responsibilities.

questions.title: challenge assumptions, clarification
questions.question: Why should you challenge assumptions and ask for clarification during an AI planning discussion?
options: Because language models will permanently erase their memory if you agree with them.
To intentionally slow down the project until deadlines expire.
To expose hidden constraints, avoid vague requirements, and discover unexpected insights.
questions.feedback: Having an interactive dialogue where you challenge assumptions and ask for clarification turns planning into a true thinking partnership. Rather than passively accepting the AI's first generic outline, probing deeper helps you uncover unstated constraints, refine goals, and discover valuable alternative approaches. The {{opt:b}} option is wrong because catching misunderstandings early prevents costly rework. The {{opt:a}} option is nonsense. In technical projects, asking 'What edge cases might break this plan?' often reveals critical security and performance requirements that initial prompts omitted.

questions.title: pitch, emerging, compelling
questions.question: A developer prepares a pitch for an emerging IoT networking tool. How does delegation support this project?
options: AI can research market comparisons and draft slide outlines, while the developer crafts the compelling core argument.
The developer bans all digital tools and writes the pitch on stone tablets.
The developer lets AI present live to investors while he sleeps.
questions.feedback: Developing a compelling project pitch for an emerging technology benefits from strategic task distribution. An AI assistant can rapidly gather comparative data, structure talking points, and draft presentation slides. Meanwhile, the developer uses domain insight to refine technical claims, anticipate skeptical stakeholder questions, and deliver the core narrative. The {{opt:c}} option is an irresponsible abdication of professional duties. The {{opt:b}} option is an exaggerated rejection of technology. Strategic collaboration allows engineers to build persuasive technical proposals in hours instead of days.

questions.title: anticipate, manageable, specify
questions.question: What should a project leader do when anticipating potential bottlenecks in an AI delegation plan?
options: Cancel the project immediately whenever any task requires more than two steps.
Anticipate failure modes, specify clear verification checkpoints, and keep high-risk tasks manageable.
Ignore all risks and assume the AI will automatically fix broken production servers.
questions.feedback: When planning multi-step projects, anticipating challenges allows you to design specific verification gates and fallback procedures. For example, if an AI agent generates script syntax, the plan should specify automated unit tests and manual diff review before merging. The {{opt:c}} option assumes magical infallibility, which causes catastrophic outages when models hallucinate. The {{opt:a}} option exhibits unnecessary fear of multi-step complexity. Proactive planning ensures that unexpected AI errors become manageable learning checkpoints rather than project-stopping disasters. By setting up sandboxed environments, developers can test agent-generated configs safely without risking production downtime.

questions.title: specify, through the lens of, substantial
questions.question: Why does saving your delegation plan matter for the upcoming Description, Discernment, and Diligence modules?
options: Because you will execute the same plan across future lessons, practicing how to specify prompts, evaluate outputs, and ensure diligence.
Because course certificates are only awarded to students who keep 1,000 text files on their Desktop.
Because future lessons will forbid you from writing any new prompts or code.
questions.feedback: The delegation plan created in this lesson serves as the practical backbone for the rest of the course. In upcoming weeks, you will specify precise instructions for each subtask using Description, critically review generated artifacts with Discernment, and verify safety and ethics through Diligence. The {{opt:b}} option is an absurd administrative joke. The {{opt:c}} option contradicts the course design, which requires continuous hands-on collaboration. Using one substantial project across all 4D modules turns abstract principles into durable practical muscle memory.

questions.title: clarification, compelling, manageable
questions.question: How does defining 'what success looks like' in Step 2 prevent project drift during AI collaboration?
options: It makes prompt writing completely unnecessary for the remainder of the project.
It forces the AI to automatically rewrite all internet articles in lowercase letters.
It establishes unambiguous objective criteria to evaluate whether intermediate AI drafts are moving in the right direction.
questions.feedback: Defining what success looks like provides an essential reference anchor for the entire project. When collaborating with versatile AI models, discussions can easily drift into interesting but irrelevant tangents unless you have established measurable deliverables, target formats, and success benchmarks. The {{opt:b}} option is nonsensical. The {{opt:a}} option is false because clear goals make subsequent prompt description sharper and more effective. When an AI generates draft materials, having clear criteria allows you to ask for targeted clarification and course corrections immediately.

questions.title: breakdown, substantial, manageable
questions.question: A student wants to build a tutorial for a complex deployment process. Which task breakdown best reflects strategic delegation?
options: AI executes root commands directly on production routers without saving a tutorial text.
Human outlines the deployment sequence, AI drafts step-by-step commands, human validates commands in a test lab, AI formats markdown.
Human writes every single letter by hand and uses AI only to calculate 2 + 2.
questions.feedback: This breakdown represents optimal delegation synergy. The engineer outlines the technical flow based on real architecture knowledge, the AI expands the outline into well-formatted explanatory prose, the engineer verifies every command in a sandbox lab, and the AI finalizes the markdown formatting. The {{opt:a}} option bypasses tutorial creation and risks catastrophic outages. The {{opt:c}} option severely underutilizes AI capabilities. Strategic delegation balances speed in content generation with rigorous human technical verification. Dividing tasks this way allows technical writers and engineers to publish comprehensive documentation in a fraction of the traditional time.

questions.title: challenge assumptions, clarification, emerging
questions.question: What is the primary advantage of exploring project planning through conversational dialogue rather than static prompt submission?
options: Iterative dialogue exposes edge cases, prompts clarifying questions, and stimulates emergent problem-solving ideas.
Static single-turn prompts are legally banned in software architecture work.
Conversational dialogue reduces the electrical power needed by cloud data centers.
questions.feedback: Conversational planning is far more powerful than single-turn prompt submissions because it enables dynamic bidirectional refinement. When you invite the AI to ask clarifying questions, challenge your assumptions, and propose alternative breakdowns, the collaborative exchange surfaces unconsidered trade-offs and edge cases. The {{opt:c}} option is an absurd claim about energy physics. The {{opt:b}} option is factually untrue. Multi-turn planning transforms AI from a basic text autocomplete tool into a genuine intellectual partner, sharpening your vision before implementation begins. In complex infrastructure design, this dialogue helps identify network latency bottlenecks and security constraints early.

questions.title: specify, breakdown, anticipate
questions.question: How does thorough project planning in Delegation directly empower the next competency: Description?
options: Delegation planning eliminates the need for written communication in all future steps.
It guarantees that the AI model will never need any further input or evaluation.
Knowing the exact task breakdown and required outcomes enables you to specify context-rich, unambiguous instructions during Description.
questions.feedback: The 4D competencies build sequentially upon one another. Thorough planning in Delegation defines exactly what subtasks exist, who is responsible for each, and what success criteria apply. This clarity directly empowers Description, allowing you to specify rich context, clear formats, and explicit constraints without hesitation. The {{opt:a}} option contradicts the framework, as Description relies on articulate prompt writing. The {{opt:b}} option is false because collaboration requires ongoing discernment. Without solid delegation planning, prompts become vague and outputs require endless correction.
